name: levea-mcp-server
description: MCP server for the Levea autonomous AI video editor — natural-language video editing (viral clips, captions, vertical reframe, chroma key, audio cleanup, motion tracking, B-roll, voiceover, music, MP4 export) for Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, Cline, OpenClaw, and Hermes.

autonomous_edit.description: PRIMARY EDIT TOOL. Run a natural-language video edit end-to-end. The backend agent plans, executes, verifies, and exports. Accepts anything from a one-liner ("generate 3 viral clips with captions and export") to a multi-paragraph creative brief. Returns the final mp4 URL synchronously when an export is queued. For long renders you may prefer queue_edit + check_job_status.

prompt.description: Natural-language description of the desired edit or creative brief. The backend planner decomposes it into canonical actions (viral clips, captions, reframe, export, …). Send the user's intent verbatim — do not pre-decompose.

project_id.description: Optional project id for tracking and continuity. Reuse the projectId returned by the first call for every continuation.

video_url.description: Optional public source video URL (HTTP/HTTPS: S3, Google Drive public link, Dropbox, direct MP4) for a new project. A local file path cannot be read directly: upload the file first (with the MCP server: call asset_upload_url, PUT the bytes to uploadUrl, then pass the returned fileUrl here).

assets.description: Optional input media assets. URLs must be public HTTP/HTTPS links; upload local files first (with the MCP server: asset_upload_url, then use the returned fileUrl).

url.description: Publicly accessible HTTP/HTTPS URL to the video, image, or audio asset.

scene.description: Optional existing scene/timeline state to continue editing (advanced).

captionTemplatePreset.description: Optional caption template to apply when (re)generating captions: a builtin slug (e.g. hormozi, mrbeast, viral-pop, karaoke, neon-pop, subtitle-bar) or a user-saved template id. With the MCP server, list_caption_templates lists the exact ids.

requirePlanApproval.description: If true, the backend stops after planning and returns workingMemory for user approval. Resend with workingMemory (and optionally editedPlan) to continue.

workingMemory.description: Working memory returned by an awaiting-approval call; resend it to resume.

editedPlan.description: Optional pre-edited plan object returned by a prior awaiting_approval response.

planDecision.description: Typed approval of a plan returned by an awaiting_approval response. Send "approve" together with the workingMemory (and optionally editedPlan) from that response to run the plan as proposed. Omit it to revise the plan with a new prompt instead.

attachedImages.description: Optional reference image URLs used for planning.

style_reference_url.description: Optional link to a style-reference video (YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, Drive, or a direct file URL). The editor downloads and measures it (cuts, beats, caption look, transitions, grade) and edits the user's footage to match its style. Its footage, wording, logos and music are never reused. Use this instead of pasting the link into the prompt when the link is a reference, not footage to edit.

skills.description: Optional list of your own skill ids ("user/<slug>", from save_skill / search_skills { mine: true }) to apply to this edit: each playbook guides the editing agent, and the style it sets (brand_id, caption_template, style_reference_url) is used where this request sets none. Skills saved with apply: always are applied automatically.

flaggedIssues.description: Optional list of specific user-flagged problems for this run (e.g. ["caption #3 misspelled"]).

brandId.description: Optional per-call brand profile id (brand kits are managed in the Levea studio or with the MCP server's brand-kit tools).

projectBrandId.description: Optional default brand for the project. Persists; per-call brandId overrides.

core_only.description: Return rendering-essential scene fields only (smaller payloads).

export_url.description: Direct URL to finished MP4 render

autonomous_edit_streaming.description: Same as autonomous_edit but consumes the SSE event stream from the backend. Returns the final terminal result; per-step events (status, thinking, tool_call, tool_result, background_job_completed) are emitted as MCP progress notifications when the client supports them. Use for long-running briefs where users expect live progress.

create_shader_effect.description: Save a reusable ShaderFX (ABI v2 / v3) effect to your effect library. source is WGSL that defines fn fx(c: FxCtx) -> vec4<f32> returning straight (non-premultiplied) rgba; FxCtx = { uv (0..1 canvas, top-left), px, res (render-target px), time = local_time (seconds since the effect layer started), progress (transition: 0→1 across the overlap; else time / layer length), intensity, frame (v3) }. Predefined helpers: src(uv), backdrop(uv), clip_a(uv), clip_b(uv), param(i), param_color(i), hash2, noise2, fbm, luma, rotate2, plus a named accessor per manifest param (P_strength() …; float → f32, vec2/vec3 → vec2/vec3<f32>, color → vec4<f32>, bool → f32 0/1). The server wraps and validates it (naga) before storing: on failure nothing is saved and errors come back as [{ line, column, message }] in YOUR source lines — fix and resend. Returns effect_id and the param table (name, type, slot, accessor). overwrite: true replaces your effect of the same name. Source ≤ 24 KB (v3: 48 KB); keep loops bounded. v3 (auto when used): textures, feedback, multi-pass, data, geometry (instanced particles / sprites). Full contract + worked examples: load_skill shaderfx-effects.

source.description: Author WGSL defining fn fx(c: FxCtx) -> vec4<f32> (plus any helper fns of your own). No bindings, no @fragment.

manifest.description: Effect manifest: { abi: 2, kind: "filter" | "transition" | "generator", output: "add" | "normal" | "replace", params: [{ name, type: "float" | "vec2" | "vec3" | "color" | "bool", min?, max?, default }] }. Slots: float/bool 1, vec2 2, vec3/color 4 (vec3/color start on a 4-slot boundary); total ≤ 32. kind defaults to filter, output to normal. Leave abi out: the server picks v3 automatically when a v3 field is present (an explicit abi: 3 is rejected). ABI v3 adds passes: [{ name, scale?: 1 | 0.5 | 0.25 }] (≤ 4; source defines fn pass_<name>(c), read with buf_<name>(uv)), textures: [{ name }] (≤ 4; tex_<name>(uv)), feedback: { enabled, warmup_sec?, clear? } (prev(uv)), geometry: { mode: "quads" | "points", count } (source defines fn instance(i, c) -> FxInstance and optional fn shade(p, c)).

textures.description: [ABI v3] Up to 4 named textures: [{ name, layer_id | asset_url, space?: "canvas" | "image" }]. layer_id = that layer rendered alone (canvas space by default); asset_url = a public png/jpg/webp ≤ 4096² (image space by default, e.g. sprite sheets). Read with tex_<name>(uv), tex_size_<name>().

layer_id.description: Layer whose picture is the texture.

space.description: Sampling space (default canvas for layer_id, image for asset_url).

feedback.description: [ABI v3] { enabled: true, warmup_sec?: 0..4 (default 1), clear?: [r, g, b, a] }: prev(uv) reads this layer's previous output frame (trails, echoes). Previews re-render warmup_sec before the frame. { enabled: false } turns a saved effect's feedback off.

data.description: [ABI v3] Up to 16384 floats for data(i), data_len(), data_vec2(i), data_vec4(i) (charts, per-instance state, lookup tables).

data_url.description: [ABI v3] Public http(s) / gs:// URL of a JSON array (or { data: [...] }) or CSV, resolved to floats at apply time (inline data wins).

geometry.description: [ABI v3] { mode: "quads" (default) | "points", count: integer 1..65536 }: draw count instanced quads; the source defines fn instance(i: u32, c: FxCtx) -> FxInstance (pos canvas uv, size px, rotation rad, color, uv_rect, alive <= 0 culls) and optionally fn shade(p: FxPixel, c: FxCtx); no fx needed. Default shade: soft round point x color, or the first texture through uv_rect x color.

overwrite.description: Replace your existing effect with the same name.

export_url.description: Direct URL to finished MP4 render

list_shader_effects.description: List the ShaderFX effects in your library (id, name, description, kind, output, params). Pass an id to apply_shader_effect.

export_url.description: Direct URL to finished MP4 render

apply_shader_effect.description: Put a ShaderFX (ABI v2) effect on a project, committed immediately. Either a saved effect (effect_id) or inline source + manifest (validated first; errors come back with line/column). kind (optional: request, else manifest, else inferred from the layer ids) "filter": target_layer_id = the layer whose picture src() reads (omit = everything composited below); window = start_time/end_time, else the target's, else the whole timeline. "transition": from_layer_id (clip A) + to_layer_id (clip B); progress runs 0→1 across their overlap. Clips meeting at a cut get a duration_sec overlap (default 0.8 s) laid on media handles, program length unchanged; SHADER_FX_NO_HANDLES if neither clip has media beyond the cut (overlap them first or shorten duration_sec). "generator": paints on its own. params = values by manifest name; param_keyframes animates them. v3 inputs: textures, feedback, data / data_url, geometry. Then check with render_preview before export.

project_id.description: Project whose committed scene is edited.

source.description: Inline author WGSL (alternative to effect_id; needs manifest).

manifest.description: Inline manifest (with source); may declare v3 passes / textures / feedback / geometry.

kind.description: Effect kind; match the manifest kind.

target_layer_id.description: [filter] Layer whose picture is src(); omit for the composited backdrop.

params.description: Param values by manifest name, e.g. { "strength": 0.8, "tint": "#ffcc66", "direction": [1, 0] }. Unknown names are errors; floats clamp to min/max.

textures.description: [ABI v3] Up to 4 named textures: [{ name, layer_id | asset_url, space?: "canvas" | "image" }]. layer_id = that layer rendered alone (canvas space by default); asset_url = a public png/jpg/webp ≤ 4096² (image space by default, e.g. sprite sheets). Read with tex_<name>(uv), tex_size_<name>().

start_time.description: [filter/generator] Timeline seconds the effect starts (ignored for transitions).

end_time.description: [filter/generator] Timeline seconds the effect ends (ignored for transitions).

duration_sec.description: [transition] Overlap length in seconds (default 0.8, at most half the shorter clip).

By default returns a compact answer: language, duration_sec, word_count, speakers, transcript_id and one page of sentence lines "[start s–end s] [speaker] text" in source seconds. detail "words" returns words with only text / start / end / speaker, paged with offset / limit; detail "full" returns the raw transcription record (very large).

detail.description: lines (default): sentence lines with start / end times. words: word-level text / start / end / speaker, paged. full: the raw transcription record (very large; avoid).

search_tools.description: Search every directly callable editing action, the read/inspection tools, AND preset catalogs (216 caption templates, 368 GPU VFX effects, 168 transitions, color LUTs, title cards, fonts, blend modes) by keyword, category, or catalog filter. With a query, matching actions come back WITH their parameter specs (required params end in "*"), so you usually do not need get_action_schema. Also returns the editorialPlaybook (fastest call pattern + NLE order). Call once with no query to see the whole surface.

catalog.description: Optional catalog filter: "captions" (216 caption templates), "vfx" (368 GPU effects), "transitions" (168 transitions), "color_presets" (LUTs), "title_cards", "fonts", "blend_modes", "properties", "animatable", "actions", or "all" (default).

limit.description: Max actions to return (default: all matches; preset catalogs default to 50).

include_schemas.description: Force parameter specs on (true) or off (false). Default: on when 25 or fewer actions match.

offset.description: Page through a long result: pass the nextOffset a previous answer returned (answers stay under ~10k tokens).

detail.description: "summary" (default): one-line descriptions. "full": full action descriptions (pages sooner).

export_url.description: Direct URL to finished MP4 render

get_action_schema.description: Fetch the full JSON inputSchema, parameter constraints, and description for any canonical editor action (e.g. COLOR_GRADE, TRIM_LAYER, GENERATE_CAPTIONS, PLAN_MOTION_GRAPHICS, RENDER_PREVIEW, EXPORT_VIDEO) or read tool (e.g. list_layers, query_transcript, inspect_layer).

action.description: Canonical action name or read tool name.

actions.description: Several action names at once (up to 40) — one round trip instead of many. They share one answer budget (~10k tokens): small schemas come whole, larger ones summarised (listed in `compacted`; schemaDetail.paramsOmitted names the rest).

params.description: Only these parameters, in full (nested schemas, every enum value): ["name", ...], or { "ACTION": ["name", ...] } per action with actions: [...]. Use it for the parameters a summarised schema lists in schemaDetail.paramsOmitted.

detail.description: "summary" (default): a very large schema is compacted to stay under ~10k tokens. "full": the whole schema as stored (CREATE_LAYER / UPDATE_LAYER are 200-380 KB).

export_url.description: Direct URL to finished MP4 render

execute_action.description: Execute any single canonical editor action (all 195 actions) or read/inspection tool (timeline_view, list_layers, inspect_layer, query_transcript, list_sources, search_shots, shot_timeline, read_source_transcript, measure_audio, measure_picture, measure_color) directly on a project scene without autonomous_edit. Pass video_url or assets on the first call to bootstrap a new project. Params accept references (@last, @primary, @all:<kind>, @end-3 …) so no id lookups are needed. Parameters are checked before anything runs (INVALID_PARAMS lists every problem with suggestions); dry_run: true checks without running. For several edits use execute_batch.

action.description: Canonical action name (e.g. REGISTER_REMOTE_ASSET, SET_SOURCE_RANGE, TRIM_LAYER, REMOVE_SILENCES, CONFIGURE_CANVAS, VERTICAL_REFRAME, COLOR_GRADE, APPLY_VFX, TITLE_CARD, PLAN_MOTION_GRAPHICS, GENERATE_CAPTIONS, STYLE_CAPTIONS, CLEAN_AUDIO, GENERATE_VOICEOVER, GENERATE_MUSIC, ADD_SFX, AUTO_DUCK, RENDER_PREVIEW, EXPORT_VIDEO) or read tool name (e.g. list_layers, query_transcript).

action_params.description: Parameters for the canonical action (see get_action_schema).

project_id.description: Project id for state persistence across calls.

video_url.description: Optional source video URL to seed a new project.

assets.description: Optional media assets to seed a new project.

include_scene.description: If true, include the full raw scene JSON in the response (omitted by default in favor of liveLayers).

idempotency_key.description: Optional: your own id for this logical call. Resending with the same key returns the first answer instead of applying the edit twice (a resend of a call that answered "running" is deduplicated even without one).

rerun.description: true runs an identical call again on purpose instead of returning the earlier answer.

dry_run.description: true: check every step's parameters against its schema (unknown names, enum values, types, ranges) in under a second and return valid / problems / corrected_params; nothing runs or is committed. Send the same call without dry_run to run it.

allow_unknown_params.description: true runs the call even with parameters an action does not take (they are ignored and listed). Default false: any parameter problem refuses the call with INVALID_PARAMS before anything runs.

export_url.description: Direct URL to finished MP4 render

execute_batch.description: Execute an ordered array of canonical actions and/or read tools in one round trip without autonomous_edit — the fastest way to edit. Pro path for any edit that picks or reorders content (shorts, highlights, recuts): 1) seed once (video_url / assets; reuse the returned project_id on every later call) and read source_map — the WHOLE source in one reply (timed sentence lines per ~1-min section + measured loudness, pauses, speaker turns, shots), not page one of the transcript; 2) PLAN_EDITORIAL_CUT — a story plan: hook with a specific promise in the first 3 s, setup, a payoff that resolves the hook, ending (optionally HOOK_CANDIDATES to rank rendered openings); 3) ASSEMBLE_PICTURE_EDIT from that plan; 4) finishing batch (reframe, captions, B-roll via bin_search inserts so cutaways show the words being said, music + AUTO_DUCK, SFX, grade) — send it with dry_run: true first, then the same batch without it; 5) VERIFY_EDIT depth "editorial" — a critic that watches and hears the render and returns fixes for hook, payoff, arc, pacing, B-roll fit, captions, mix; apply them; 6) EXPORT_VIDEO (its polish gate fixes safe craft issues and returns a polish report). Surgical tweaks (one caption colour, one trim) skip straight to the batch. History: UNDO / REDO step one version; restore_version { revision } or { label } jumps to a saved version or checkpoint (undoable, no confirmation); name versions with checkpoint { label }; try alternatives with fork_variant / compare_variants / promote_variant (pass variant beside project_id to edit a variant). The whole batch is validated first: an unknown, non-callable or unconfirmed destructive action (destructive ones need confirm_destructive: true), and any parameter an action does not take or a value outside its enum / type / range (INVALID_PARAMS), rejects it before anything runs, listing every problem with did-you-mean suggestions; declared aliases are corrected and reported in corrected_params. Exact names: get_action_schema (several actions in one call). Up to 25 steps; atomic: if a step fails while running nothing is committed (allow_partial: true keeps the steps that succeeded). The response has a receipt per step. After the edits the server runs structural passes only (safe zones, timeline reconciliation) — never creative additions — and commits the scene to project_id. Results are unverified: check them with render_preview. EXPORT_VIDEO as the last step masters loudness automatically if MASTER_AUDIO was not called. Answers stay under ~10k tokens: a long read output in a batch is paged (its receipt names the start / offset that continues) and replyBudget lists anything shortened. query_transcript returns timed sentence lines (detail: "words" for per-word times); timeline_view is compact on a busy timeline (detail: "full" for every field).

actions.description: Ordered list of { action, params } steps to execute.

project_id.description: Project id for state persistence across calls.

video_url.description: Optional source video URL to seed a new project.

assets.description: Optional media assets to seed a new project.

include_scene.description: If true, include the full raw scene JSON in the response (omitted by default in favor of liveLayers).

idempotency_key.description: Optional: your own id for this logical call. Resending with the same key returns the first answer instead of applying the edit twice (a resend of a call that answered "running" is deduplicated even without one).

rerun.description: true runs an identical call again on purpose instead of returning the earlier answer.

dry_run.description: true: check every step's parameters against its schema (unknown names, enum values, types, ranges) in under a second and return valid / problems / corrected_params; nothing runs or is committed. Send the same call without dry_run to run it.

allow_unknown_params.description: true runs the call even with parameters an action does not take (they are ignored and listed). Default false: any parameter problem refuses the call with INVALID_PARAMS before anything runs.

allow_partial.description: false (default): atomic. true: commit every step that succeeded. "until_failure": commit the steps before the first failure.

confirm_destructive.description: Required true for destructive actions (CLEAR, DELETE_LAYER on many layers, …).

export_url.description: Direct URL to finished MP4 render

render_preview.description: Render real GPU-composited JPEG screenshots of the live project timeline at specified timestamps (and optional normalized 0..1 region crop) — the Levea equivalent of ffmpeg frame extraction, showing all video layers, captions, title cards, color grades, masks, and VFX shaders. Returns native MCP image blocks so you can visually inspect the frames before calling EXPORT_VIDEO.

timestamps.description: Timeline timestamps in seconds to capture (e.g. [1.0, 5.0, 12.0]).

region.description: Optional normalized zoom region { x, y, width, height } in 0..1 coordinates.

tools.name: autonomous_edit
tools.description: PRIMARY EDIT TOOL. Run a natural-language video edit end-to-end. The backend agent plans, executes, verifies, and exports. Accepts anything from a one-liner ("generate 3 viral clips with captions and export") to a multi-paragraph creative brief. Returns the final mp4 URL synchronously when an export is queued. For long renders you may prefer queue_edit + check_job_status.

tools.name: autonomous_edit_streaming
tools.description: Same as autonomous_edit but consumes the SSE event stream from the backend. Returns the final terminal result; per-step events (status, thinking, tool_call, tool_result, background_job_completed) are emitted as MCP progress notifications when the client supports them. Use for long-running briefs where users expect live progress.

tools.name: queue_edit
tools.description: Fire-and-forget async path. Returns immediately with a `taskId`. Use when the edit may exceed the MCP request timeout (long viral-clip generation, multi-format export). Poll with check_task_status or get_active_task.

tools.name: create_shader_effect
tools.description: Save a reusable ShaderFX (ABI v2 / v3) effect to your effect library. source is WGSL that defines fn fx(c: FxCtx) -> vec4<f32> returning straight (non-premultiplied) rgba; FxCtx = { uv (0..1 canvas, top-left), px, res (render-target px), time = local_time (seconds since the effect layer started), progress (transition: 0→1 across the overlap; else time / layer length), intensity, frame (v3) }. Predefined helpers: src(uv), backdrop(uv), clip_a(uv), clip_b(uv), param(i), param_color(i), hash2, noise2, fbm, luma, rotate2, plus a named accessor per manifest param (P_strength() …; float → f32, vec2/vec3 → vec2/vec3<f32>, color → vec4<f32>, bool → f32 0/1). The server wraps and validates it (naga) before storing: on failure nothing is saved and errors come back as [{ line, column, message }] in YOUR source lines — fix and resend. Returns effect_id and the param table (name, type, slot, accessor). overwrite: true replaces your effect of the same name. Source ≤ 24 KB (v3: 48 KB); keep loops bounded. v3 (auto when used): textures, feedback, multi-pass, data, geometry (instanced particles / sprites). Full contract + worked examples: load_skill shaderfx-effects.

tools.name: list_shader_effects
tools.description: List the ShaderFX effects in your library (id, name, description, kind, output, params). Pass an id to apply_shader_effect.

tools.name: apply_shader_effect
tools.description: Put a ShaderFX (ABI v2) effect on a project, committed immediately. Either a saved effect (effect_id) or inline source + manifest (validated first; errors come back with line/column). kind (optional: request, else manifest, else inferred from the layer ids) "filter": target_layer_id = the layer whose picture src() reads (omit = everything composited below); window = start_time/end_time, else the target's, else the whole timeline. "transition": from_layer_id (clip A) + to_layer_id (clip B); progress runs 0→1 across their overlap. Clips meeting at a cut get a duration_sec overlap (default 0.8 s) laid on media handles, program length unchanged; SHADER_FX_NO_HANDLES if neither clip has media beyond the cut (overlap them first or shorten duration_sec). "generator": paints on its own. params = values by manifest name; param_keyframes animates them. v3 inputs: textures, feedback, data / data_url, geometry. Then check with render_preview before export.

tools.name: delete_shader_effect
tools.description: Delete a saved ShaderFX effect from your library. Layers that already use it keep their own copy of the shader.

tools.name: check_job_status
tools.description: Poll an export / async job by jobId (numeric). Supports wait:true to block until terminal.

tools.name: check_task_status
tools.description: Poll a queued edit task by taskId (returned by queue_edit), or a direct tool call that answered status "running" (taskId "dc_…" from execute_action / execute_batch / render_preview: waits up to ~25 s for it, and its result is that call's full response once status is completed / failed). Direct calls already wait for their own result, so you rarely need this. Separate from job_id (exports).

tools.name: get_active_task
tools.description: For a given project, return the currently-running edit task (if any). Useful for reconnecting MCP clients.

tools.name: list_caption_templates
tools.description: List the user's caption templates (builtin + saved). Returns slugs, display names, and style summaries.

tools.description: Apply a caption template to a scene synchronously (without going through autonomous_edit).

tools.description: Transcribe an existing asset (cached after the first call). By default returns a compact answer: language, duration_sec, word_count, speakers, transcript_id and one page of sentence lines "[start s–end s] [speaker] text" in source seconds. detail "words" returns words with only text / start / end / speaker, paged with offset / limit; detail "full" returns the raw transcription record (very large).

With a query, matching actions come back WITH their parameter specs (required params end in "*"), so you usually do not need get_action_schema. Also returns the editorialPlaybook (fastest call pattern + NLE order). Call once with no query to see the whole surface.

tools.name: get_action_schema
tools.description: Fetch the full JSON inputSchema, parameter constraints, and description for any canonical editor action (e.g. COLOR_GRADE, TRIM_LAYER, GENERATE_CAPTIONS, PLAN_MOTION_GRAPHICS, RENDER_PREVIEW, EXPORT_VIDEO) or read tool (e.g. list_layers, query_transcript, inspect_layer).

tools.name: execute_action
tools.description: Execute any single canonical editor action (all 195 actions) or read/inspection tool (timeline_view, list_layers, inspect_layer, query_transcript, list_sources, search_shots, shot_timeline, read_source_transcript, measure_audio, measure_picture, measure_color) directly on a project scene without autonomous_edit. Pass video_url or assets on the first call to bootstrap a new project. Params accept references (@last, @primary, @all:<kind>, @end-3 …) so no id lookups are needed. Parameters are checked before anything runs (INVALID_PARAMS lists every problem with suggestions); dry_run: true checks without running. For several edits use execute_batch.

tools.name: execute_batch
tools.description: Execute an ordered array of canonical actions and/or read tools in one round trip without autonomous_edit — the fastest way to edit. Pro path for any edit that picks or reorders content (shorts, highlights, recuts): 1) seed once (video_url / assets; reuse the returned project_id on every later call) and read source_map — the WHOLE source in one reply (timed sentence lines per ~1-min section + measured loudness, pauses, speaker turns, shots), not page one of the transcript; 2) PLAN_EDITORIAL_CUT — a story plan: hook with a specific promise in the first 3 s, setup, a payoff that resolves the hook, ending (optionally HOOK_CANDIDATES to rank rendered openings); 3) ASSEMBLE_PICTURE_EDIT from that plan; 4) finishing batch (reframe, captions, B-roll via bin_search inserts so cutaways show the words being said, music + AUTO_DUCK, SFX, grade) — send it with dry_run: true first, then the same batch without it; 5) VERIFY_EDIT depth "editorial" — a critic that watches and hears the render and returns fixes for hook, payoff, arc, pacing, B-roll fit, captions, mix; apply them; 6) EXPORT_VIDEO (its polish gate fixes safe craft issues and returns a polish report). Surgical tweaks (one caption colour, one trim) skip straight to the batch. History: UNDO / REDO step one version; restore_version { revision } or { label } jumps to a saved version or checkpoint (undoable, no confirmation); name versions with checkpoint { label }; try alternatives with fork_variant / compare_variants / promote_variant (pass variant beside project_id to edit a variant). The whole batch is validated first: an unknown, non-callable or unconfirmed destructive action (destructive ones need confirm_destructive: true), and any parameter an action does not take or a value outside its enum / type / range (INVALID_PARAMS), rejects it before anything runs, listing every problem with did-you-mean suggestions; declared aliases are corrected and reported in corrected_params. Exact names: get_action_schema (several actions in one call). Up to 25 steps; atomic: if a step fails while running nothing is committed (allow_partial: true keeps the steps that succeeded). The response has a receipt per step. After the edits the server runs structural passes only (safe zones, timeline reconciliation) — never creative additions — and commits the scene to project_id. Results are unverified: check them with render_preview. EXPORT_VIDEO as the last step masters loudness automatically if MASTER_AUDIO was not called. Answers stay under ~10k tokens: a long read output in a batch is paged (its receipt names the start / offset that continues) and replyBudget lists anything shortened. query_transcript returns timed sentence lines (detail: "words" for per-word times); timeline_view is compact on a busy timeline (detail: "full" for every field).
